latest_release.name: @effect/openapi-generator@4.1.6
latest_release.body:
### Patch Changes

- [#10799](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/10799) [`66ab992`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/66ab9920271ee7fec3be3f4e3b4438d9222578b1) Thanks @gcanti! - Generated client method comments now show the OpenAPI operation summary above the description, with identical text appearing only once.

- [#10921](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/10921) [`60ae98e`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/60ae98eed32ec80625bb9a54008f74f10ab8f329) Thanks @CheckPickerUpper! - Generated HttpApi groups now drop the group prefix from endpoint names (`balance.read` becomes `read`) while keeping the qualified OpenAPI operation id, reject operations whose names collide within a group, and only emit the parameter schemas grouped endpoints use.

- [#10839](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/10839) [`cf50541`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/cf50541d0deaa1f21df91e938b94eadbe10dd274) Thanks @Marve10s! - Fix generated `multipart/form-data` payloads rejecting `format: binary` files in open object schemas while preserving undeclared form fields.

- [#10797](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/10797) [`f90a026`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/f90a026c0b8acfc062c40b553025d226eba670a2) Thanks @gcanti! - A response with no body can still have a description in the API documentation. For example, an OpenAPI file can describe a `404` as "Order not found". The generator used to copy the status code into the `HttpApi` and drop that text.
  
  ```ts
  // Before
  HttpApiSchema.Empty(404)
  
  // After
  HttpApiSchema.Empty(404).annotate({ description: "Order not found" })
  ```
  
  Exporting the generated `HttpApi` back to OpenAPI now produces the original "Order not found" description.
  
  ### A shared `404` with its own description
  
  In this OpenAPI 3.1 example, `$ref` points to a shared response whose description is "Resource not found". The line below it gives this particular `404` a more specific description.
  
  ```yaml
  responses:
    "404":
      $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
      description: Order not found
  ```
  
  The generator writes `HttpApiSchema.Empty(404).annotate({ description: "Order not found" })`. If you omit the `description` line, it uses "Resource not found" from the shared response.
  
  ### An explicit `500` and a fallback
  
  ```yaml
  responses:
    "200":
      description: OK
    "500":
      description: Server error
    default:
      description: Other errors
  ```
  
  For this input, the generated endpoint has one error response, `HttpApiSchema.Empty(500).annotate({ description: "Server error" })`. The generator skips `default` and emits a warning because it would assign "Other errors" to the same status. If you remove the explicit `500` from this example, the generator uses `default` to produce a `500` described as "Other errors".
- Updated dependencies [[`dd5f2f3`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/dd5f2f322fbad042a3a186cef593bf42affe5ce9), [`1d65846`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/1d65846308a6a18c4a95af543988ad30b72ff2b3), [`694c28f`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/694c28f0cfc3eac33f71160d18dda95cb670f506), [`5aaa2cd`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/5aaa2cd216e5e55f92d06db98d4b54946a396eed), [`55814bf`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/55814bf0a780f05ed0a51c82c8affda5d539bb0e), [`92c40a1`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/92c40a1f96a59f9edcacee6c0d6f6fb80397ee17), [`9f415a7`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/9f415a7733cdf8aed7efadbed3b5db22890e164a), [`e367afd`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/e367afdacfa3041a694a67e4670e98a20e41d45c), [`d5d2112`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/d5d21120ff591fcf8da006ce340010812cc91f16), [`fa2e5af`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/fa2e5af4ccc8f3650d97049707be82eab098c168), [`6bf6427`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/6bf6427d195539c387c13156aff79db077929c8f), [`10bc4a4`](http

# Effect

Effect is a library for building robust, maintainable, type-safe, and production grade applications in TypeScript. It helps you handle the hard problems at scale: typed errors, dependency injection, structured concurrency, scheduling, tracing, and unified schema validation.

> **Effect 4.x is a long-term support (LTS) release.** If you are upgrading from Effect 3.x, follow the [migration guide](MIGRATION.md).

## Installation

```sh
npm install effect
```

## Requirements

- **TypeScript 5.9 or newer.** TypeScript 7 is recommended for the best performance and compatibility with [Effect's TypeScript tooling](https://github.com/Effect-TS/tsgo#installation).
- **Node.js 22.19 or newer** is the general minimum for running Effect on Node.js.
- **Strict type-checking:** the `strict` flag must be enabled in your `tsconfig.json`.

## Links

- [Website](https://effect.website): documentation, guides, and news
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/effect-ts): ask questions, share what you're building, and talk to the core team
- [Community](https://effect.website/community-hub): meetups and events, or bring Effect to your own
- [Issues](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues): bug reports and feature requests
- [Jobs](https://effect.website/effect-jobs): companies hiring Effect developers
- Follow us on [X](https://x.com/EffectTS_), [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/effect-ts.bsky.social), and [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/effect-ts)

## Let's talk

Whether your team is considering Effect, rolling it out, or already running it in production, we'd love to hear from you: what you're building, what works, and what you need from Effect next.

- **Talk to the maintainers.** Introduce your team on [Discord](https://discord.gg/effect-ts) or email [contact@effectful.co](mailto:contact@effectful.co). We're happy to connect privately on Slack or Discord for feedback and help with adoption.
- **Production support.** We're exploring how to better support teams running Effect in production. If your organization has specific support needs, let's discuss them.
- **Adoption help.** Our [adoption partners](https://effect.website/adoption-partners) offer implementation, consulting, team extension, training, and commercial support.

Feedback from teams using and evaluating Effect directly shapes what we stabilize and build next.

## Long-term support

Teams depend on Effect for systems they expect to run for years. Effect 4.x is a long-term support (LTS) release with the following guarantees:

- At least three years of support, including bug and security fixes.
- Bug fixes for one year after the next major version is released.
- Security fixes for two years after the next major version is released.

Stable APIs reserve breaking changes for major releases. APIs marked unstable may change in minor releases, and experimental APIs may change in patch releases.

## Effect v3

The Effect v3 source code is available on the [`v3`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/tree/v3) branch, which is also where issues and pull requests meant for Effect v3 should be targeted. To upgrade, see the [migration guide](MIGRATION.md).
